title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
authors: Guibin Zhang, Leo Lu, Fangzhou Xie (core contributors); Kang Zhu, Junhao Wang, Zhifei Xie, Zhaochen Yu, Zihang Liu, Zhongxiang Sun, Qiankun Li, Yue Liao, Heng Chang, Xiaobin Hu, Qibing Ren; corresponding Wangchunshu Zhou, Chuanrui Hu, Yafeng Deng, Shuicheng Yan
lab: National University of Singapore, EverMind AI, Nanyang Technological University (v2; v1 was signed "LV-NUS Lab" and listed only Zhou and Yan as corresponding)
date: 26 August 2026 (arXiv v1); revised 3 September 2026 (v2, the version this page links)

code.title: bingreeky/JIT, MIT
code.note: The inference runtime (generate three harnesses, pick one, run it, score it), the HarnessFactory seed harnesses (11 of the paper's 13), adapters and data for seven of the nine benchmarks (not BrowseComp-Plus or PinchBench). No training code for the three stages and no streaming archive. The 27B checkpoint is on Hugging Face (Apache 2.0), as are 2,852 of the training harnesses

takeaway: Makes harness construction a trained capability: factor any harness into (Memory, Planning, Action, Capability orchestration), then train a 27B model (Qwen3.6-27B, SFT plus repair supervision plus evolutionary GDPO against a harness archive) to synthesise, repair, and evolve one per task at inference time; +7.7 avg for GLM-5.2 and +8.8 for DeepSeek-V4-Flash across nine agent benchmarks, enough for a harnessed V4-Flash to beat bare GPT-5.6, at 14.9-54.1% lower cost than fixed harnesses.
verdict: Believe that a harness written for each task can beat five off-the-shelf harnesses on score and cost on three benchmarks, and that the released code and model let anyone check. Treat the size of the gains as provisional: every number is one run with no error bars, most margins that can be tested sit inside sampling noise, nothing turns the three training stages or the archive off, the "vanilla" scaffold behind Table 2 is never described, and the largest gains come on DeepPlanning, where 520 of the 2,852 released training harnesses were written for the test cases' own databases (new requests, no copied test query).

resources.t: GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization
resources.n: the method Evo-GDPO adapts: GRPO applied to a sum of several rewards collapses distinct reward combinations into identical advantages; normalising each reward separately keeps them apart.

resources.t: Meta-Harness: end-to-end optimization of model harnesses
resources.n: the ahead-of-time approach JIT-Agent argues against: search for one durable harness from traces, then keep it.

kb.t: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
kb.n: Asks whether untrained frontier models can build and evolve a harness; their evolution steps helped held-out scores only about half the time. JIT-Agent claims the same skill can be trained, but never measures evolution step by step.

kb.t: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
kb.n: The mirror image: it gives an untrained model a rich harness and notes models are not trained to operate it; JIT-Agent trains a model to build the harness but keeps the harness simple. Neither has done both.
The hand-built harness whose lift JIT-Agent tries to automate; StateM's versioned YAML runbook is roughly a hand-tuned (M, P, A, F) instance.
The F module is the skills question; the 10% skill-misapplication rate found there is a plausible source of residual failures. In the released training harnesses, F mostly exposes every tool.

kb.t: Learn What's Left, Not What's Mastered (SA-MRPO)
kb.n: The same multi-objective RL problem as Evo-GDPO's three channels, approached by saturation-aware reweighting rather than frontier comparison.
Another way to make the capability layer learnable: distil repositories into skills. Like JIT-Agent, its headline gains need checking against what each result actually used.
Uses the serving harness as a training curriculum; like JIT-Agent it ablates none of its own components.
The baseline harness of Figure 4 and the first row of the seed bank: full history, no planner, the ReAct loop, every tool.
Where group-relative advantages come from; Evo-GDPO keeps the group but normalises each reward channel separately.
Stage I's preference step is DPO weighted by the size of the reward, latency and cost gap.
